note: He is the sharpest illustration in this batch of the stated ICP pulling in two directions. On starting point he is a perfect fit and the rep said so on the call - 'a lot of people are already like, kind of go from like good to great... it sounds like you're in the good to great category' - and at 47 with roughly 10-12% body fat, a six pack and daily training he is the furthest thing from the deconditioned exclusion. But he misses the three criteria that determine whether a deal happens. He is a high school English teacher, not a business owner or physician; his income does not clear the bar, which he stated plainly and the rep endorsed ('you get paid what you get paid regardless'); and health is not his neglected area at all - it is the one part of his life he has kept in order for five years, which is why there was no problem for the offer to solve. Judged against the criteria as written rather than against the outcome, he is outside, and the outcome agreed. The finding worth carrying up is that the stated ICP has no way to express what he actually was: an ideal programme fit and a poor commercial fit, wanting a mid-tier product the company does not sell.
